title: Performance & Load Validation
method: dependency-free ThreadPoolExecutor+requests load harness (reports/p8_6_evidence/loadtest*.py) against the live docker-compose stack, concurrency levels 1/10/25/50

backend_auth_login.note: correctly rate-limited (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10/window) under load, all requests beyond the first few returned 429 as designed; reported as security-control validation, not a latency measurement

bottleneck_identified.finding: no --workers flag (defaults to 1 process); under concurrency-50 sustained load, CPU plateaued at ~1.1 of 8 available logical cores while throughput plateaued at 135-190 rps
bottleneck_identified.root_cause_classification: real, observed performance bottleneck (not a functional defect: 0 errors, graceful latency degradation, no corruption)
bottleneck_identified.why_not_fixed_this_phase: DEVICE_BACKEND=memory is process-local; adding --workers would shard the in-memory device store across processes and cause real 404 DEVICE_NOT_FOUND regressions for devices registered by a different worker. DEVICE_BACKEND=postgres would need to become the default first -- an architectural decision outside this phase's narrow performance-validation scope.
bottleneck_identified.recorded_as: Suggested Improvement for a future phase

failure_under_load: 0 errors across ~5000+ total load-test requests this phase; genuine failure-injection (stopping device-ai/backend mid-session) already covered live in P8.5 SS10-11, not duplicated here

test_accounting.note: measurement/validation phase only; no application test files added, removed, or modified

environmental_limitations: Load levels bounded by single dev-machine capacity (8 cores, shared with OS and unrelated local containers) -- not necessarily representative of dedicated production headroom
Single-machine ThreadPoolExecutor load generation, no distributed load generator, no 100s-1000s concurrency ceiling test attempted (out of scope for pilot-readiness)
Live Hyperledger Fabric transaction latency not measurable -- no live peer in this environment, unchanged since P6.2/P8.2
